title: Criterion Channel — Art-House Horror
read_scope: official search-index description; direct open geo-blocked
support: formal experimentation and horror coexist with strange beauty
limit: curatorial grouping, not a universal visual recipe or a current availability claim

title: David Church — Post-Horror
support: elevated/post-horror and cultural distinction are debated critical categories
limit: book not read in full; no inference of artistic superiority

title: Noel Carroll — The Nature of Horror
support: monster abnormality relative to the fictional world; philosophical use differs from arthouse grouping
limit: summary does not establish every claim of Carroll theory

title: Freud Museum — The Uncanny
support: familiarity, doubles and animation of inanimate figures
limit: psychoanalytic interpretation, not a diagnosis or a measurable pixel emotion

title: Masahiro Mori — The Uncanny Valley
read_scope: authorized English translation of original essay; appearance and movement sections
support: hypothesis concerning human likeness and affinity; movement is a distinct variable
limit: one still cannot measure a valley in an audience response curve

title: Julia Kristeva — Powers of Horror
support: abjection and the instability of subject/object boundaries
limit: not a synonym for blood, dirt, or disgusting texture

title: Mark Fisher — The Weird and the Eerie
support: weird/eerie are related but distinct modes, not intrinsically horrifying
limit: publisher description alone does not support detailed definitions

title: Mark Fisher — authorized book extract and introduction
read_scope: introduction quoting Fisher, lines 219-223; surrounding author extract
support: weird presence that does not belong; eerie failure of presence/absence
limit: distinguish quoted Fisher definition from editorial introduction; empty place alone does not prove a missing agent

title: MoMA Learning — Glossary of Art Terms
read_scope: selected Expressionism, Grotesque, Avant-garde glossary entries
support: distorted forms and color; incongruous form; experimental practice
limit: historical movements are not certified by one isolated shape

title: MoMA — Surrealism
read_scope: official indexed definition; direct page has section headings and works
support: historical movement, dreams and unexpected object/material combinations
limit: new scene designs are research proposals, not descriptions of listed works

title: MoMA — Biomorphic
read_scope: official indexed definition; direct page work list
support: abstract forms evoking organisms or body parts
limit: organic appearance does not establish living tissue

title: The Met — Symbolism
support: subjective ideas/emotions through form, line and composition
limit: not a universal symbol dictionary or evidence of viewer response

title: National Gallery — Vanitas
support: still-life organization relating achievement and mortality
limit: any still life containing a skull is not automatically the full historical genre

title: National Gallery — Memento mori
support: reminders of death across portraits, still lifes and saints
limit: broader theme than the vanitas still-life type

title: The Met — Relics and Reliquaries in Medieval Christianity
read_scope: museum essay, container and body-part reliquary sections
support: container versus contents; precious exterior; body-shaped containers
limit: object appearance cannot authenticate relic identity or sacred status

title: BFI — 10 great body horror films
support: mutation, transformation, bodily control and autonomy differ from gore quantity
limit: film examples do not make every body variation a horror marker

title: Erin Harrington — Women, Monstrosity and Horror Film: Gynaehorror
read_scope: official indexed publisher description and topic list; direct open unavailable
support: reproductive, maternal and sexual embodiment includes nonreproductive bodies
limit: book not read in full; female or pregnant appearance does not itself imply monstrosity

title: Barbara Creed — The Monstrous-Feminine, second edition
read_scope: official indexed publisher description and contents; direct open unavailable
support: critical analysis of cultural constructions; updated feminist/nonhuman readings
limit: not a biological category or a command to sexualize women

title: Laura Mulvey — Visual Pleasure and Narrative Cinema
read_scope: official journal metadata: Screen 16(3), 1975, pp 6-18, DOI 10.1093/screen/16.3.6; full text unavailable
support: bibliographic primary-text pointer for gaze analysis
limit: the argument has not been reread here; detailed claims require primary-text review before integration

title: Laura U. Marks — The Skin of the Film
support: haptic visuality engages embodied memory; situated in intercultural cinema
limit: a texture close-up is a possible application, not proof of touch, smell or cultural experience

title: Michel Chion — Audio-Vision: Sound on Screen
support: sound-image relations concern an audiovisual channel
limit: book description not a complete glossary; still-image audio claims remain unverified

title: Oklahoma State — Introduction to Film and TV: Sound
read_scope: official university indexed textbook excerpt; direct open 403
support: diegetic sources belong to the story world; sound perspective and asynchronous sound
limit: visible radio or reaction does not prove an audible event

title: Columbia Film Language Glossary — Mise-en-Scene
support: organized shot elements and staged artificial environment
limit: the pedagogical scope is broad; do not conflate every use with a strict staging-only definition

title: National Gallery — Tenebrism
support: selected illuminated details against a predominantly dark setting
limit: not mere underexposure or a synonym for all chiaroscuro

title: FilmColors — Suspiria (1977)
read_scope: archive metadata and print credits, lines 23-35
support: different material prints and color systems have distinct provenance
limit: no stills visually reviewed; exact RGB values and native movie pixels not verified

title: BFI — Pleasures and pains of the flesh
read_scope: critical essay, terminology and autonomy passages
support: New French Extremity as a critical grouping; differentiated bodily agency
limit: not all grouped films or directors share the same politics

title: MoMA — Cinemas of Transgression
support: specific punk/No Wave underground lineage
limit: not every work that breaks a taboo belongs to this movement

title: BFI — 10 great erotic horror films
support: desire, death and transgressive cinema are intersecting analytical concerns
limit: a visible material, proximity or wound does not establish sexual intent

title: Nitsch Museum — Ritual
support: ritual, repetition, procession and performance props as organized form
limit: photograph of a tableau does not establish actual sacrifice or participation consent

title: Columbia Film Language Glossary — Camera Movement
support: camera movement is a temporal film technique
limit: a still image cannot establish movement or its speed

title: Columbia Film Language Glossary — Lighting
support: light organization is separable from narrative genre
limit: color patches alone do not prove fixture type or psychological effect

title: Columbia Film Language Glossary — Long Take
support: shot duration and continuity require temporal observation
limit: cannot be certified from a single image

title: Marina Abramovic — Rhythm 0
read_scope: MoMA transcript including artist testimony, lines 6-19
support: documented performance, duration and spectator participation
limit: a still tableau cannot reproduce duration or infer consent from passivity

title: Stadel Museum — Viennese Actionism
support: historically specific expansion of painting through material action
limit: red paint and real animal remains are distinct media; no automatic substitution

title: Hyundai Artlab — Mire Lee, Open Wound
read_scope: commission metadata, captions and project text
support: commissioned installation; industrial space and organic-looking materials
limit: Tate direct pages inaccessible; actual installation pixels not reviewed

title: NCMA — Tableau Vivant
support: posed living picture as an organized scene
limit: posed people do not prove long-duration stillness

title: BFI — Skinamarink
support: domestic setting and suspended spatial/narrative expectations
limit: interpretive film analysis, not generated-pixel qualification

title: Japan Foundation — Hijikata Tatsumi Archive interview
read_scope: official indexed interview opening and archive account
support: specific Butoh lineage and archival performance evidence
limit: not a generic ghost-dance preset; full interview not read

title: MoMA — Institutional critique
support: critique of institutions and power surrounding circulation/display
limit: a price label or gallery alone does not establish critique

title: MoMA — Modern Art and Ideas glossary
support: performance art and institutional critique are different art practices
limit: no complete PDF or artwork-pixel review

title: BFI — 40 years of Suspiria
support: neon-colored nightmare fairy tale and links to staged cinema
limit: not a requirement for all art horror or giallo

title: Criterion — Eyes Without a Face
support: 1960 Franju film; surgery, beauty and lyrical/ghastly juxtaposition
limit: synopsis does not certify every scene or make masks substitute for injuries

title: Criterion — Eraserhead
support: 1977 Lynch film; black-and-white photography and sound design
limit: still-image dataset cannot certify sound design

title: MoMA — Under the Skin
support: 2013 Glazer film; spare cinematography and electronic soundscape
limit: synopsis interpretation is separate from still-image observation

title: A24 — Midsommar
support: 2019 Aster film; couple, festival and threatening narrative context
limit: synopsis alone does not independently establish lighting details

title: National Gallery — Chiaroscuro
support: tonal contrasts, volume and modelling; different uses by Leonardo and Caravaggio
limit: not synonymous with all tenebrism or a complete physical lighting setup

title: MIT Press — Yve-Alain Bois
support: bibliographic pointer to Bois and Krauss, Formless: A Users Guide
limit: no direct verification of the book argument or Bataille original
